subject: Business Models
title: Platforms vs Pipelines
description: A quick, practical guide to Platforms vs Pipelines.

hook.text: Traditional businesses are pipelines: make a thing, sell a thing. Platforms don't make anything at all.

buildup.text: A pipeline company like Toyota builds cars. A platform like Uber connects drivers to riders.

discovery.text: Platforms create value by enabling exchanges. They own the marketplace, not the inventory.

twist.text: The world's largest taxi firm owns no cars. The largest hotel chain owns no rooms. Platforms won.

climax.text: Platforms scale faster because adding users costs nearly zero, while pipelines must build more factories.

punchline.text: Own nothing, connect everyone. That's the platform model.

quiz.question: What is the key difference between platforms and pipelines?
options: Platforms enable exchanges rather than making products
